To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we can infer offensiveness in images from natural language supervision; (2) this is done by selecting the most relevant prompt for a given image; (3) we use CLIP for this; (4) the results are better than the state-of-the-art.

(1) pre-trained transformers can be used to automatically curate datasets, (2) the curation of image datasets can be improved by using a prompt-based approach, and (3) our approach can be used to detect offensive images.

(a) we propose a new task for the automated culling of large-scale datasets based on the supervision from human-annotated data; (b) we demonstrate that this task can be solved with a pre-trained transformer; and (c) we provide a methodology for evaluating the offensiveness and diversity of large-scale image datasets.
